text:
Maya: Heads up — noticed when we revoke a service account key, some requests still succeed for ~30s due to edge cache TTL. Product expects near-immediate 401s.
Tony: Yeah, edge caches TTL is 30s. We can shorten but risk thundering on control plane. We should consider invalidation propagation instead of shrinking TTL.
Maya: Filed an internal ticket but wanted to discuss: could we surface a console metric for 'stale-auth-success' or 'revocation-lag' so SRE/product can see impact in real time?
Sasha: We currently emit auth_denied and auth_ok but can't tell if auth_ok was for a revoked key. Need an explicit signal: auth_ok/with_revoked_flag=false|true depending on whether edge saw revocation.
Liam: Control plane receives revocation webhook and writes marker to central DB. Proposal: publish a short-lived invalidation event (pub/sub) that edges subscribe to so they can invalidate caches immediately.
Tony: Pub/sub works but ops will flag scaling: ~200k active keys and bursts during org-wide rotation. Cross-region delivery and fanout cost needs review.
Zoe: Could we hybridize? Push immediate invalidation to region of origin and rely on eventual sync elsewhere. Console should show per-region propagation status.
Maya: UX idea: a "Revocations" panel listing key, org, initiated_at, per-region status (pending/success/failed), and propagation percentiles. Also a small timeline for last 5mins.
Sasha: Telemetry requirement: emit auth.invalidation.latency (ms) with tags region, method=pubsub|poll, outcome=success|fail. Also count invalidation_failures.
Tony: There's a quota angle too — if revoked requests continue and get queued, they might still increment metering. We need to ensure revoked keys stop counting immediately.
Liam: Fix in metering pipeline: attach revocation sequence to usage events; consumers check latest revocation seq for key before accepting. If usage.seq <= revoked.seq then drop.
Maya: Can we demo a simple flow in staging? Steps: revoke key -> expect invalidation event -> edge drops cache -> next request 401 -> console shows propagation success.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: auth-invalidation-refactor v2 -> staging
Tony: FYI, ran a quick staging run. Median propagation in us-west ~120ms with pubsub, tail <1s. Poll fallback ~2.5s median.
Zoe: What's the fallback/circuit-breaker plan if pubsub saturates or pauses? Edge should gracefully revert to polling TTL and we should surface that in console.
Liam: Add config flag edge.auth.invalidation.strategy = pubsub|poll and edge.auth.invalidation.last_success_at metric. Also edge should log invalidation_failed key=<id> reason=<err> for tracing.
Sasha: For alerts: fire when per-region 99th percentile invalidation latency > 5s or when revocation-failure-rate > 0.5% for >5m. Also correlate with auth_ok_after_revocation spikes in dashboards.
Maya: Action items I captured:
- liam: implement pubsub plumbing + polling fallback, prod-scale test
- tony: update metering pipeline to drop revoked usage events
- sasha: add telemetry metrics + alerts, update dashboards (revocations panel)
- maya: mock console wireframe + rollout plan (canary to low-QPS orgs first)
Zoe: +1 to canary low-QPS first. Also document rollback: disable pubsub, revert edge flag to poll, and re-enable TTL if needed.
Tony: One more: API docs need a note about expected revocation visibility and SLOs. Security/compliance teams will ask for guarantees.
Maya: Great. I'll sync with security on SLO wording. Thanks everyone — will follow up with PR links and the wireframe tomorrow.
Sasha: :thumbsup:
Liam: assigning tasks in linear -> @Tony, @Sasha, @Maya
Zoe: thanks, logging this for oncall runbook updates.
